subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes, prompt layer, redaction, observability, and Codex-native skill interactions are allowed?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but selecting explicit/default/auto behavior and deciding what trusted skill material may cross into external harness prompts is a product and security boundary decision.

options.title: Design the ACP contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt lifetime, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to existing skill filters
options.body: Do not add a per-spawn selector yet; rely on agent-level skill filters and current harness-specific behavior until the broader prompt contract is settled.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Close or route future work outside core if maintainers decide ACP harnesses should not receive OpenClaw-rendered skills through `sessions_spawn`.

recommendation.title: Design the ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt lifetime, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the central ACP thread-bound spawn surface and merged later related ACP session-boundary work.
